About the project

Runoregi is a Web-based user interface for browsing a large corpus of Finnic tetrameter poetry. In addition to combining several independent collections, it also provides innovative similarity detection and visualization algorithms, allowing the user to quickly move between related texts, read similar texts in a side-by-side view, find occurrences of lines and passages regardless of linguistic variation, and more.

The corpus currently combines the following collections:

  • Suomen Kansan Vanhat Runot (Old Poems of the Finnish People; SKVR)
  • Eesti Regilaulude Andmebaas (Estonian Runosongs Database; ERAB)
  • The Finnish Literature Society's Corpus of unpublished poems (JR)
  • A Corpus of literary poems (KR) based on public domain sources.

Runoregi was developed within the research project “Formulaic intertextuality, thematic networks and poetic variation across regional cultures of Finnic oral intertextuality, thematic networks and poetic variation across regional cultures of Finnic oral poetry” (FILTER) funded by the Academy of Finland grant no. 333138 (2020-2024). It remains an actively developed research prototype and is provided as-is, without any guarantee of stability or correctness of neither methods nor data. The users are encouraged to double-check the materials from SKVR, ERAB and JR collections with their official user interfaces.

Source code

The source code of Runoregi and all related tools is publicly available. It can be divided as follows:

User interfaces

  • runoregi – the Runoregi user interface
  • filter-visualizations – the Visualizations user interface (maps and type indices)

The back-end pipeline for creating database:

  • filter-pipeline – preprocessing and similarity computation
  • filter-db – converting CSV tables to a MariaDB database
  • filter-data – the intermediate dataset in CSV format (output of filter-pipeline, input to filter-db)

Libraries containing computational methods:

  • matrix-align – optimized sequence alignment computation for large datasets
  • shortsim – a Python library and toolkit for string similarity computations

Citing

If you use Runoregi in your research, please cite:

  • Maciej Janicki, Kati Kallio & Mari Sarv (2022). Exploring Finnic written oral folk poetry through string similarity. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities. https://doi.org/10.1093/llc/fqac034

Contact

  • Maciej Janicki, University of Helsinki (code and computational methods)
  • Kati Kallio, Finnish Literature Society (Finnish collections)
  • Mari Sarv, Estonian Literary Museum (Estonian collections)

Privacy policy

Runoregi does not use cookies or store any data on the user's computer.

This instance collects usage data for diagnostic purposes. The collected data includes the address of the requested page and information about the user's browser and operating system.
